mechanism_principle.content: Spiral states in NiI2/frustrated lattices are governed by a delicate competition among intralayer exchanges: Heisenberg exchange together with anisotropic interactions such as Kitaev/biquadratic terms stabilize an incommensurate spiral, and the spiral wavevector is highly sensitive to the balance among J1, J3, and K.

It is seen that for J3 > 0 (AFM), the competition of these intralayer exchanges resulting an incommensurate (IC) spin spiral, whose wavevector q is sensitive to specific values of J3 and K.

evidence_spans: This behavior is attributed to enhanced interlayer exchange coupling that progressively rebalances the competition among the frustrated intralayer J1–J3–K interactions.

evidence_spans: Our calculations show that it arises from local curvature induced modification of intralayer J3/J1 interactions.

At wrinkles, additional nonuniform structural deformation is imposed locally, which further changes the Ni-I bond lengths and bond angles (the Ni-I bonds are compressed in the inner side and stretched on the outer side, as shown in Fig. S6 (online)) [19, 56]. Since the spin-spiral wavevector is determined by a delicate balance among these competing interactions, such local structural perturbation can shift the preferred wavevector and lead to the observed deflection.

The curvature-induced deflection of spin spirals reveals a different mechanism, where curved surface perturbs the intralayer exchange interactions locally. evidence_result.content: Spin spiral modulations consistent with a canted-plane spin spiral are observed in NiI2, in line with prior STM studies; across a step edge between adjacent terraces, the modulation persists but the phases are nearly reversed.
evidence_spans: We note similar spin modulations have been reported in several prior STM studies of monolayer NiI2 [30, 34-36], which are confirmed to be a spin spiral state with canted rotation plane [34].
Fig. 2f shows an SP-STM image across a step edge. The spin spiral modulation exists in different terraces, while the phases of spin modulation between two adjacent terraces are nearly reversed.

evidence_result.content: Atomic-resolution HAADF-STEM directly resolved two distinct stacking orders in the film.
evidence_spans: The atomic-resolved HAADF images clearly resolved two different stacking orders, as shown in Fig. 1e and f.

evidence_result.content: The spin spiral state undergoes sharp reorientation at nanoscale wrinkles, showing that local curvature/strain can deflect the spin spiral.
evidence_spans: Second, we found the spin spiral state undergoes sharp reorientation at nanoscale wrinkles of the film.

evidence_result.content: Curvature-induced spin-spiral deflection is common across samples, with deflection angles mainly 40°–68%; simulations of a curved monolayer show a clear ~60° deflection in the curved region, qualitatively matching experiment, whereas a flat-lattice simulation does not show such regular deflection.
evidence_spans: We have examined various samples and confirmed that such local curvature induced deflection of spin spiral is a common behavior (see Part Ⅰ-4 of Supplementary Material for additional data). The deflection angle of spin spirals in curved regions is mainly distributed in the range of 40°–68°.

Fig. 5h shows the simulated spin texture of the curved lattice, which exhibits a clear deflection of spin spirals (with an angle of ~ 60°) in curved region. This is qualitatively consistent with the experimental observation in Fig. 5c and d.
For comparison, Fig. 5g shows the simulation of a non-curved lattice, where no such regular deflection is observed

evidence_result.content: On the curved lattice, the absolute values of J3/J1 and K are reduced in the curved region, providing a microscopic basis for the observed spin-spiral deflection.
evidence_spans: As shown in Fig. 5i and j, on the curved lattice, the J3/J1 ratio and K show notable reduction of their absolute values in the curved region.

evidence_result.content: No robust topological charge is found in the spin-spiral deflected region.
evidence_spans: No robust topological charge is found at the deflected region.

evidence_result.content: NiI2 films on NbSe2 exhibit spin-spiral wavevectors similar to those on HOPG despite markedly different interfacial charge transfer, indicating the wavevector is not strongly altered by substrate-dependent charge transfer.
evidence_spans: As shown in Part Ⅰ-5 of Supplementary Material, NiI2 films grown on NbSe2 substrate still exhibits spin-spiral wavevectors similar to those on HOPG, even though their dI/dV spectra indicate significant difference in interfacial charge transfer.

evidence_result.content: A reduced 2×2×2 Γ-centered k-point mesh was tested and did not affect the conclusions.
evidence_spans: A reduced 2×2×2 Γ-centered k-point mesh was also tested, and the results showed no impact on the conclusions.

evidence_result.content: Overall, the study systematically demonstrates that both thickness and local strain/curvature govern the spin-spiral state in van der Waals multiferroic NiI2.
evidence_spans: we have systematically unveiled the effects of thickness and local strain on the spin spiral state in vdW multiferroic NiI2.

constraint.content: A 15 Å vacuum buffer was imposed along the non-periodic axis to avoid interlayer interactions.
evidence_spans: To avoid interlayer interactions, a vacuum buffer of 15 Å is implemented in the non-periodic axis.
